description: Market cap, P/E, P/B, P/S, EV/EBITDA, EV/revenue and dividend yield on a share price YOU supply (1 to 25 per call), joined to point-in-time SEC EDGAR filings. A share price is never a Valuein figure: pass one only when the user gave it to you, or a tool the user connected returned it in this conversation; never from memory. Each row needs the price date, the close, its currency and (for the record) where it came from in `source_label`, e.g. your market-data provider, broker export or internal price database. RULES: a price joins only filings accepted BEFORE it was observed (default 16:00 New York on `price_date`); a ticker means the company that held it ON `price_date`; splits effective after the filing and on or before the price date are applied to the filed share count and per-share figures, and a split between period end and filing is not (the filing already holds it); a company with more than one listed share class gets no multiple at all (`multi_class_price_needed`); a price in another currency needs `fx_rate`; a `total_return` close is refused; a `split_adjusted` close needs `adjusted_through`. OUTPUT per price: `metrics`, `metrics_display` (QUOTE VERBATIM), `metrics_provenance` (each figure's `derived_id`, the filed `fact_id`s behind it and `rests_on: ["user_supplied_price"]`), `metrics_unavailable` (why a figure is null), `warnings`, and `price_inputs_echo` (the price exactly as you sent it, `basis: "user_supplied"`). When you write a figure that rests on a price, state the price and its date beside the figure and call it user-supplied; cite the `derived_id` so `verify_facts` can re-run it. The price is never called current. Check that your price and the filing use the same share basis; a split missing from the corporate-action table is not detected. Nothing is stored. Use `as_of_date` to cap the filings used.

as_of_date.description: Optional cap, YYYY-MM-DD: only filings accepted before the end of this day are used, even when a price is later.

prices.description: 1 to 25 prices, one per company and date.

adjusted_through.description: For split_adjusted: the date the adjustment runs to (YYYY-MM-DD).

adjustment.description: How the close was adjusted; default raw. split_adjusted needs adjusted_through. total_return is refused for multiples.

as_of.description: When the price was observed, ISO 8601 with offset. Default: 16:00 America/New_York on price_date.

cik.description: SEC Central Index Key of the company. Preferred over a ticker.

close.description: Closing price per share, in `currency`: above 0, at most 10,000,000, at most 8 decimal places.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency of the close, e.g. USD.

fx_rate.description: Units of the company's reporting currency per 1 unit of `currency`; needed when the currencies differ. Also yours.

price_date.description: Date the close belongs to, YYYY-MM-DD. Required: a price without a date is refused.

source_label.description: Your own note on where the price came from, at most 64 characters. Shown as yours.

ticker.description: Ticker, resolved to the company that held it ON price_date (recycled tickers map by date).

name: compute_price_multiples

_meta.description: Provenance envelope — data lineage for every MCP response

cost_usd.description: Per-call cost transparency. Omitted for subscription-only and free tools, which have no MPP price.

basis.description: mpp_charge = real pay-per-call charge (a card or MPP payment through agent-pay). mpp_rate_card = indicative price, not billed.

billed.description: true = this amount was actually charged via MPP for this call. false = indicative MPP-equivalent value only: no charge was made for this call (it was within your plan).

data_plan.description: Access plan: sample | sp500 | pro | full

data_quality.description: Server-side invariants run on this response

fundamentals_as_of.description: ISO timestamp when the FINANCIAL STATEMENTS were last rebuilt in bulk. Use THIS — not `last_updated` — when telling a user how current the cross-sectional fundamentals are. The snapshot is republished on every weekday price refresh while the statements are carried forward unchanged, so `last_updated` can be far more recent than the numbers it sits next to. It is a floor for a single filer, not a ceiling: a filer with a live partition receives its filing, facts and ratios intraday (minutes after EDGAR dissemination), so an entity-scoped read may carry a filing newer than this; cross-sectional ranks (factor scores, earnings signals) refresh with the weekly bulk export.

last_updated.description: ISO timestamp when the snapshot was exported

latency_ms.description: Wall-clock milliseconds this tool call took, measured server-side around the handler.

limit_warnings.description: Soft-warning array for partial fulfillment. Each entry carries a stable subcode + remediation.options[]. AI agents pattern-match on subcode.

mpp_offer.description: Present when figures still need payment: the MPP option (price, resource_url, request body) for the full run.

mpp_override.description: Set when this single response was paid for over MPP (card, agent-pay): the payment's order was honoured for this call only. agent-pay captures the payment only when this is present.

mpp_verification.description: Verification tools only, when some figures are outside the caller's plan. Figures the plan covers are always verified free; a Valuein account also verifies its first figures free, once, figures outside its plan included (the verification trial, size in pricing://current). served_free = own-plan figures plus trial figures; trial_used / trial_remaining = this run's draw and what the account has left; needs_payment = figures still to pay for (the paid verification run). A guest has no trial: note says how to get it.

pit_safe.description: true iff a zero-look-ahead point-in-time cut was applied to every returned figure

reset_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the window resets

truncation.description: Set when fewer rows were returned than requested — explains why and points to a remedy
